name: Question 20
problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at  $a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ ∗\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ \\ ∗ & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=2{x}_{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2{x}_{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+\pi +(-1)=\pi -1.
$$

Question 20

Consider the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[x1+x22sin⁡(x1+x2)],x=[x1x2].

If the linear approximation of f at a=[π2π2] is given by

f(x)≈[π2+π24∗]+[1∗∗−1](x−[π2π2]),

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
3π4+1
b
π+1
c
π
d
π2
e
π−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x1+x22)=1,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x1+x22)=2x2∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(sin⁡(x1+x2))=cos⁡(x1+x2),∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(sin⁡(x1+x2))=cos⁡(x1+x2)

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[12x2cos⁡(x1+x2)cos⁡(x1+x2)].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[π2π2], we have

f(a)=[π2+π240],f′(a)=[1π−1−1].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[π2+π240]+[1π−1−1](x−[π2π2]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

0+π+(−1)=π−1.
